Foxsports.com All-Freshman Team (2010) }} '''Xavier Henry''' (born March 15, 1991) is an American [[basketball]] player. Henry is a 6'6" guard from [[Oklahoma City, Oklahoma]], [[United States]]. He is a freshman at [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]]. ==Personal== Xavier Henry was born in [[Ghent]], [[Belgium]], where his father played professional basketball in the early 1990s.Jenni Carlson. "[http://newsok.com/article/3212515/1204780472 Xavier Henry has plenty of reasons to keep smiling]". NewsOK.com. March 6, 2008. Retrieved on April 4, 2009. Henry's brother, [[C. J. Henry|C. J.]], is a freshman on the University of Kansas basketball team. He was a [[2005 Major League Baseball Draft|2005 MLB draft]] first round pick and returned to college after playing three years of [[minor-league baseball]] in the [[New York Yankees]] and [[Philadelphia Phillies]]' organizations.Pete Thamel. "[http://www.nytimes.com/2007/07/09/sports/ncaabasketball/09henry.html?_r=1&scp=7&sq=Xavier+Henry&st=nyt&oref=slogin A Top Prospect Could Turn Into a Package Deal]". ''New York Times''. July 9, 2007. Retrieved on March 21, 2009. The brothers' father, [[Carl Henry (basketball)|Carl]], played basketball at [[University of Kansas|Kansas]] in the 1980sBrandon Lilly. "[http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2008/highschool/01/03/xavier.henry/ Bracing for success: Putnam City's Henry appears ready for the next step]". ''Sports Illustrated''. January 8, 2008. Retrieved on March 21, 2009. and their mother played basketball for the Kansas women's team.[http://collegebasketball.about.com/od/recruiting/p/xavier-henry.htm Mom Played Basketball in College] ==High School== Henry was named to the 2009 [[McDonald's All-American Team]] where he scored 14 points.[http://seattletimes.nwsource.com/html/highschoolsports/2008969865_webhoopagatewed02.html? syndication=rss Wednesday's McDonald's All-American Game box scores] Henry was also selected to play in the 2009 [[Nike Hoop Summit]] at the [[Rose Garden (arena)|Rose Garden]] in [[Portland, Oregon|Portland]] where he led Team USA with 22 points including six [[3 pointers]][http://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/content.asp?CID=934728 World stars surprise USA at Nike Hoop Summit] and the Jordan Brand Classic at [[Madison Square Garden]] where he scored 10 points for the white team.[http://sports.espn.go.com/highschool/rise/basketball/boys/news/story?id=4080678 Big men shine in Jordan Brand Classic] He was ''[[SLAM Magazine]]'''s high school diary keeper for the 2008–09 basketball season.Ryan Jones. "[http://slamonline.com/online/college-hs/high-school/2009/03/xavier-henry-will-be-televised/ Xavier Henry Will Be Televised]". ''SLAM Online''. March 19, 2009. Retrieved on March 21, 2009. On March 14, 2009, he led Putnam City High School to the Oklahoma Class 6A state championship, scoring 24 points in the title game against Jenks High School.Ryan Aber. "[http://newsok.com/class-6a-boys-putnam-city-routs-jenks-for-trophy/article/3353606 Class 6A boys: Putnam City routs Jenks for trophy]". NewsOK.com. March 15, 2009. Retrieved on March 21, 2009. On October 22, 2008, Henry was in a [[car accident]] and fractured his [[cheekbone]]. He had to have surgery in November and he missed the beginning of his senior season.[http://theshiver.com/2008/11/xavier-henry-to-decide-in-the-spring/ Xavier Henry breaks cheekbone] ===Recruitment=== By the end of his senior season, Henry was ranked as the #6 overall prospect and #2 shooting guard in the class of 2009 by [[Scout.com]][http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&c=4&cfg=bb&pid=88&yr=2009 Scout Top 100], #8 overall and #3 shooting guard by [[Rivals.com]][http://kansas.rivals.com/viewrank.asp?ra_key=1642 Rivals Top 150] and #3 overall, #2 shooting guard by [[ESPN]].[http://insider.espn.go.com/ncb/recruiting/tracker/espnu100?&season=2009 ESPNU 100] Originally, Henry was heavily recruited by both [[University of Memphis|Memphis]] and [[University of Kansas|Kansas]]. On Nov. 18, 2008 Henry announced his commitment to Memphis citing the opportunity to play alongside his brother, C.J., as the primary reason for the decision.[http://www2.kusports.com/news/2008/nov/18/henry-picks-memphis/ Henry picks Memphis] In March 2009, Memphis' head coach [[John Calipari]] took the head coaching job at the [[University of Kentucky]], prompting Henry to reopen his recruitment.James Pennington. "[http://kykernel.com/2009/03/31/father-of-no-1-recruit-xavier-henry-says-he-will-decommit-from-memphis/ Father of No. 1 recruit, Xavier Henry, says he will decommit from Memphis]". ''Kentucky Kernel''. March 31, 2009. Retrieved on April 1, 2009. On April 23, Xavier officially announced his choice to play basketball for Kansas.[http://www2.kusports.com/news/2009/apr/23/xavier-henry-announces-hes-coming-ku/ Xavier Henry announces he’s coming to KU] {{cquote|''I grew up always wanting to go to Kansas. I switched to Memphis because my brother was going there. Now, with coach (John Calipari) leaving (for Kentucky), we've decided to go to KU. I'm really excited. That's where my whole family played.''|||Xavier Henry}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2009}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Xavier Henry | position = SG | hometown = Oklahoma City, OK | highschool = Putnam City HS | feet = 6 | inches = 6 | weight = 210 | 40 = | commitdate = 4/23/2009 | scout stars = 5 | rivals stars = 5 | espn grade = 98 }} |- |} ==College== [[File:20091219 Manny Harris guarded by Xavier Henry.jpg|thumb|Henry guarding [[Manny Harris]]]] Henry scored 27 points in his first college game, breaking the record for most points scored by a Jayhawk in a debut game as a freshman.J. Brady McCollough. "[http://www.kansascity.com/sports/story/1569458.html Henry sets KU debut record for freshman with 27 points]". ''Kansas City Star''. November 13, 2009. Retrieved on November 14, 2009. On December 12, 2009, Henry scored 31 points against LaSalle at the Sprint Center in Kansas City. In doing so he became the first KU freshman to score 30 points in a game since [[Paul Pierce]]. Henry's 31 points was four short of the KU record for points scored by a freshman set by KU legend and current assistant coach [[Danny Manning]]. Gary Bedore. "[http://www2.kusports.com/news/2009/dec/13/most-excellent/?mens_basketball Henry scores 31 in rout of Explorers]". Lawrence-Journal World''. December 13, 2009. Retrieved on December 14, 2009. ==Professional career== On April 7, 2010, Henry announced that he would forgo his final three seasons of collegiate eligibility and enter the [[2010 NBA Draft]], where he is expected to be a first round selection.{{cite news|url=http://www.tsn.ca/ncaa/story/?id=317033 |title=KANSAS FRESHMAN HENRY DECLARES FOR NBA DRAFT |date=April 7, 2010 |publisher=tsn.ca.}} ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== *[http://www.kuathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/henry_xavier00.html Kansas Bio] *[http://www.nbadraft.net/players/xavier-henry NBADraft.net Profile] *[http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Xavier-Henry-1324/ DraftExpress.com Profile] *[http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=8&c=1&nid=2431349 Scout.com Profile] *[http://rivalshoops.rivals.com/viewprospect.asp?pr_key=41773&Sport=2 Rivals.com Profile] *[http://www.usabasketball.com/news.php?news_page=09_hsum_feature_henry Nike Hoop Summit Bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Henry, Xavier}} [[Category:People from Oklahoma City, Oklahoma]] [[Category:African American basketball players]] [[Category:Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Oklahoma]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:Shooting guards]] [[Category:People from Ghent]] [[Category:1991 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[fr:Xavier Henry]]
